title: Neighborhood pricing experiments - scratchpad
content:
Quick jot: neighborhood pricing = attempt to anchor microcommit tiers to observed cohort spike behavior (rather than global percentiles).

Goal: create compact, psychologically simple offers that map to real burst patterns we see in small apps (chatbots, search assistants). Not full commit (Dedicated) — lightweight reserved-ish credits + burst buckets + decay window.

Hypothesis: If we present a small predictable monthly microcommit (e.g., $9/mo) that buys a baseline of low-latency tokens + a neighbor-burst credit pool with tapering, conversion from free->paid increases because the perceived tail risk is covered.

Design primitives:
- baseline microcommit (monthly): anchors price and gives continuous SLA-ish value (slower pre-warm allowed).
- neighborhood buffer (shared burst credits): N credits usable in bursts; refill cadence daily or weekly depending on tier.
- tapering multiplier: bursts above buffer consumed at higher token price or older-burst discount removed.
- warm slot credits: short lived low-latency slots (1-5s cold start benefit) consumed for interactive sessions.

Back-of-envelope numbers (rough, aim to sanity-check with infra):
Assumptions: avg serving cost = $0.12 / GPU-hour (amortized infra) for mixed quantized models serving on shared infra, effective tokens per GPU-hr: 3M tokens/hr for small-gen usage average (short sequences + batching). So cost per token ~= $0.12 / 3,000,000 = $4e-8 ($0.00000004) per token.

Target margin accounted: want 60% gross margin for starter microtiers => price per token externally ~= cost / 0.4 => $1e-7 (0.0000001) per token. Round to easy unit: 0.0000001.

Offer sketches:  
1) Pocket ($5/mo): baseline 25k tokens included (equivalent cost ~ 25k * 1e-7 = $0.0025 -> negligible so value perception > cost). Includes 1k burst credits (counts same token unit) with taper above buffer billed at 1.6x token rate. Daily refill: none. Aim: marketing anchor.
2) Starter ($15/mo): baseline 150k tokens + neighborhood buffer 25k (refill weekly). Warm slot pool 30 slot-minutes. Overage billed at payg rate 0.0000001 / token.
3) Microcommit ($50/mo): baseline 600k tokens + buffer 200k (refill weekly) + 200 warm slot-minutes + 3x concurrency cushion. Allow small SLO on latency.

Why neighborhood buffer not simple credits? Behavioral: buffers that refill periodically create "breathing room" and are perceived as a safety valve; tapering enforces capacity discipline.

Anchoring experiments to run (A/B):
- Anchor price vs included tokens: Keep $15 but vary included baseline tokens (50k/150k/300k) and watch conversion / refund churn.
- Buffer refill cadence: daily vs weekly vs monthly (likely weekly best for conversational apps).
- Taper multiplier sensitivity: 1.2x / 1.6x / 2.0x — how does usage shift?
- Warm-slot visibility: UI showing slot pool vs silent consumption changes perceived value. Test both.

Operational heuristics for engineering:
- Implement buffer as a FIFO credit bucket with timestamped refills (simple ledger).
- Enforce taper via dynamic price multiplier on overage tokens only.
- Warm-slots should be implemented as short-lived priority tokens that run on faster instance pool; enforce soft cap and fallback to normal path.

Unit econ checks (ballpark):
- If Starter sees 50% of customers fully use baseline + 30% buffer -> expected average token consumption = 150k + 0.3*25k = 157.5k. At external price equivalence (0.0000001) revenue per Starter ~ $15 (by construction). Cost = 157.5k * 4e-8 = ~$0.0063. Gross margin ~ 99.96% (obviously unrealistic because cost assumptions too low since they ignore infra overhead, networking, storage, support). Need to replace cost with realistic blended cost (GPU amort + infra + support) say $0.005 per 1k tokens -> $0.000005 per token. Recompute: cost = 157.5k * 0.000005 = $0.7875 -> margin ~ 95%. Still high; suggests pricing can be lowered or include more value.

Need to sanity check with dedicated/different model families: high-context assistants (longer sequences) reduce tokens/hr drastically; factor by 3-5. So for those workloads neighborhood buffers should be smaller or priced differently (per-session caps).

Edge cases / questions:
- Fraud: buffer refill frequency exploitable by scripts? Add per-minute throughput caps or slot gating.
- Refunds/chargebacks: if they game burst repeatedly, we need throttles and spike detection.
- Multi-tenant pooling: do we allow teams to share buffers across subaccounts? Could be a paid feature.
- Display: show explicit "burst remaining" meter in Console and API.

Quick experiments to run with minimal infra:
1) Create 3 starter variants in billing test org, soft-launch to 500 orgs, track daily top-decile burst usage and conversion events.
2) Add telemetry for warm-slot consumption and latency delta vs fallback.
3) Implement taper multiplier in billing preview only (no charge) to gauge behavior.

Notes to self: avoid language like "commit" in marketing for micro tiers. Use "reserve" or "pocket". Keep UI simple: baseline + burst + warm-slot. Avoid per-token decimals in UI; show human friendly units (e.g., 150k tokens).

Open numbers to fetch before next iteration:
- Real blended per-token cost (infra+network+storage+support) by model class (small, medium, large) — ask infra-fin to slice.
- Actual tokens/hr observed distribution for free-tier cohorts (last 90d) — ask analytics.
- Warm slot cost delta (fast instance premium) per minute.

If this plays out, mid-tier upgrade path should map to "dedicated cushion" product (upgrade from warm slots to reserved instances).

TODO: schedule 30m with Priya and Liam to pick two variants, pick pricing copy, and set instrumentation key metrics (conversion, churn, top-decile cost).

Random scribbles:
- Consider packaging warm-slots as "fast-sessions" sold in packs (10/50/200 minutes) rather than bundled in tier. Might be more intuitive.
- Can we offer an "auto-top" for buffer refill (small instant purchase when buffer hits 10%) — frictionless revenue.
- Explore-monthly vs rolling-week refill: rolling-week simpler to explain? or say "weekly refresh".

End of notes.

-- Marina
